predecessors.name: Funj Sultanate
predecessors.text: Dar Shaigiya, "from Korti in the south to Berti Island in the north"

successors.name: Turco-Egyptian Sudan
successors.text: Dar Shaigiya, "from Korti in the south to Berti Island in the north"

ledger.x: c. 1690: the Shaiqiya break from the Funj. "Around 1690 the tribe broke loose from the Kingdom of Funj, defeating the Abdelab governor", becoming "the region's only independent tribe".
4 November 1820: the Shaiqiya are beaten at Korti.
November 1820: the independent Shaigiya end; they serve the Turkish army and are rewarded with Ja'alin land between Shendi and Khartoum after 1822.

wars.name: Battle of Korti and the Turco-Egyptian invasion
wars.outcome: Egyptian victory at Korti on 4 November 1820 and Jebel Daiqa on 2 December 1820; the Shaiqiya submit and serve the Turks.

certainty.note: A river kingdom described by its two ends, Korti and Berti Island.
